subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: English in action – Buying tickets
outcomes: Use expressions to buy tickets and ask about prices.
Work out the total price of tickets.
Hear and say the weak schwa sound in -er and -or endings.

tf.s: We say “Can I have four tickets, please?” to buy tickets.
tf.why: Yes, it is a polite way to ask.

tf.s: We ask “How much is a guide?” to find out the price.
The customer says “Here you are” when giving the money.
tf.why: Yes, we say it when we give something.

tf.s: At the fort, a guide costs ten rials.
The boy in the dialogue buys two tickets.
The boy wants a guide because he wants to know about the fort's history.
tf.why: Yes, a guide tells you about the fort.

tf.s: In operator, the last syllable has a weak schwa sound.
Two adult tickets at 7 rials and two child tickets at 4 rials cost 18 rials.
The customer says “Here are your tickets.”
tf.why: The ticket seller says that; the customer says Here you are.

boxes.why: How much asks for the price.

boxes.q: What does the customer say when giving money?
What does the seller say with the tickets?
How much is a guide at the fort?
The boy asks: Can I have ___ tickets, please?
Which word ends with a weak schwa sound?
3D cinema: adult 3 rials, child 2 rials. One adult and one child?

o: Can I have two tickets, please?
boxes.why: Can I have … please? is polite.

mcq.q: Which question do you use to ask the price?
How many tickets does the boy buy?
What does the customer say when giving the money?
mcq.why: Here you are is used when giving something.

mcq.q: Where is the schwa sound in operator?
Adult 7 rials, child 4 rials. Two adults and two children. How much in total?
3D cinema: adult 3 rials, child 2 rials. Two adults and three children want tickets. What does the seller say?
You want two tickets for children. What do you say?
o: Can I have two tickets for children, please?

mcq.q: A father and three children (child 4 rials) want a guide (10 rials). Adult is 7 rials. What is the total?
Why does the boy decide to have a guide?
o: He wants to find out about the fort and its history.
He doesn't want to buy tickets.
mcq.why: A guide can explain the fort's history.

mcq.q: Which answer is the ticket seller's line, not the customer's?
o: Here are your tickets. Enjoy the visit!
Can I have four tickets, please?
mcq.why: The seller gives the tickets and wishes you a good visit.
